themes.name: Cortado
themes.inspiredBy: One Dark Pro's balance + Ayu's warmth (caliber only)
themes.identity: Roasted-espresso brown surfaces (h 63), crema-cream text and a golden crema accent: the set's only warm-brown dark, like a café at closing time.
themes.eyeComfort: Warm, low-blue surfaces at OKLCH L 0.23 with cream text at 12.3:1 rather than 15+:1; the accent and status colours stay at chroma 0.16 or less, so nothing glows.
themes.notes: The accent is gold (h 85) and warn is orange (h 50) on purpose, ΔE 20 apart, so the accent never reads as a warning. err is crimson-pink (h 18), ΔE 21 from warn. The primary button and TXN pill carry dark espresso text. The selection is a deep amber-brown at 45 % alpha: it is visible through colour (ΔE 11 against bg), not brightness, and over the current line it stays at luminance 0.031 or less, so every existing syntax theme (Standard, Neon, …) stays at 4.5:1 on it.
themes.sqlNotes: Warm-led café palette: caramel keywords (h 70, one step warmer than the gold accent), butter numbers, rose strings, celadon functions and lilac constants that match the grid's NULL. The only cool notes are teal types, sky CTE names and slate schema prefixes, so names that point elsewhere read cool against warm structure. Comments are a near-neutral warm grey at APCA Lc 51.
themes.da1Notes: DA1: function moved from sage to celadon (was ΔE 1.2 from Standard's string, 5.8 from Monokai Pro Ristretto's function).
themes.statesNotes: The gold accent owns the amber slot, so warn moves from orange #f58b4b to apricot #ffb389 and err from salmon to rose-coral #fc8192: warn/err under tritan 3.7 -> 10.9 with warn still 16 from the accent; ok becomes grass green #73ba59 so success no longer merges with error for deuteranopes (1.8 -> 9.4). Toast/banner tint 12 %, Run 8/11.5/15 %, Stop 6/9.5/13 % keep every label >= 4.58:1; the warning row goes to 20 % so it reads apricot instead of a hovered brown row, and STAGING turns orange #ffa661 so it is not the gold accent. Dark, so neutral steps lift: default/ghost hover rises to the hairline's lightness but keeps a warm milk-coffee chroma (C .031), so it reads crema-brown, not grey, and the border brightens to #594d44. The gold primary has a dark label, so hover/pressed go lighter and creamier (#eabc6c → #f8cb80, label 10–11.7:1) instead of the muddy 85 %-black mix; danger deepens because its white label caps how light it can go. Focus (ring + field) is the accent lifted one step, #e8c67d, so a focused field stays apart from the salmon/pink error under deuteranopia (ΔE 11.6–12.7 vs 9.2 with the plain accent). Critic: pressed no longer lightens past hover (text-err fell to 4.09, the top-bar server name's text-muted to 3.80); it keeps hover's lightness and deepens toward crema (C .040), so every label a .q-btn / .q-tb carries (fg, err, accent, muted) stays >= 4.55. Warning squiggle back on its own token (#cca700, Monaco's amber): deutan dE from the error squiggle 10.5 -> 17.5, and it no longer matches bracket2 (3.9).

themes.name: Fathom
themes.identity: Deep-sea teal-navy (h 215, clearly greener than Querithm Dark's blue-grey) with an aqua accent and a neutral sea-mist foreground.
themes.eyeComfort: Neutral foreground (chroma 0.009) at 12.9:1. The aqua accent sits at chroma 0.10 instead of neon cyan, and the selection is a muted ink-blue, so the editor never flashes.
themes.notes: The selection is blue (h 245), not teal: on a teal background a teal selection was too faint (best ΔE 6.8 inside the syntax layer window), and blue reaches ΔE 10.5. ΔE to the Night Owl background is 9.1. info (sky blue) and the accent (aqua) are 18.6 apart.
themes.sqlNotes: Sea-glass keywords (h 172, greener and lighter than the aqua accent) on the cool sea; the literals are the warm notes (coral strings, sand-gold numbers, orchid-pink constants matching the grid's NULL), with sky functions, lavender types and shell-pink parameters. CTE names are a pale kelp green (ΔE 21 from identifiers, 15 from the keyword they follow) and schema prefixes a dim sand.
themes.da1Notes: DA1: parameter moved off lime (ΔE 3.0 from Night Owl's #addb67/#c5e478, 1.8 from Juniper's keyword) to shell pink. bg left in place: the deep-teal niche is boxed in by Noctis, Solarized Dark, Night Owl, Oceanic Next and GitHub Dark (no bg ≥ ΔE 6 from all exists), so Fathom's identity rests on its teal keywords + coral strings, which none of those uses.
themes.statesNotes: Ok lifts to a lighter mint #7ddd9c and err deepens a touch to #f8767a (also >= 4.5:1 on the Buttons seat btnHover, for the q-btn text-err buttons): success vs error for deuteranopes 3.7 -> 8.6 and info vs success for tritanopes 6.7 -> 8.5 come from a lightness gap, not from darker text. Toast/banner 12 % (err was 4.43:1 on raised at 15 %), Run 8/11.5/15.5 %, Stop 6.5/10/13 %; env words use the shared dark family (DEV teal-green #60d0a6 for PROD/DEV deutan 11.7). Neutral steps lift into a deeper, slightly more saturated sea-teal (#0b3b46 → #194751) rather than toward grey; the hairline is greyer, so the hover separates from its border by colour and the border brightens to #355258. The aqua primary carries a dark label, so it brightens on hover and pressed (#64d6d2 → #78e6e2, label 10.4–12.2:1); danger deepens. Focus stays the accent aqua: ≥ 4.4:1 on every surface and selection fill, ΔE ≥ 19 from the error colour in every CVD simulation. Critic: hover a hair deeper (muted 4.44 -> 4.56); pressed sinks into deeper sea-blue at hover's lightness (#00384a, h227) instead of lifting (err 3.81 -> 4.61). Warning squiggle #cca700: CVD separation from the error squiggle 12.0 -> 13.6. Note: the Run/Stop percentages in the buttons note above are stale; the values are Run 8/12/15 %, Stop 7.5/11/14 %.

themes.name: Inkwell
themes.identity: Royal violet ink (h 317, L 0.174, C 0.059): the darkest, most saturated and highest-contrast theme of the set, with ice-blue keywords, a violet accent and a teal-ink selection.
themes.eyeComfort: The highest contrast in the set is still under 15.5:1. The foreground is a neutral grey-white (L 0.92), not pure white, and the background has real chroma, so it never becomes an OLED-style near-black that halates.
themes.notes: At this lightness the background hue had to sit at least 35° from Querithm Dark (h 271), so it is violet-ink rather than blue-indigo. Its ΔE is 8.6 to Tokyo Night and 7.3 to Catppuccin Mocha. The lavender accent (h 292) is ΔE 18 from Querithm Dark's blue accent. It is the only dark theme with a white-label primary button (#6a5ec9).
themes.sqlNotes: Ice-blue keywords (h 233) are the set's only azure keyword and the cold note on violet ink; mint strings, apricot functions, lime numbers, a lilac type, pink constants, straw parameters and pale-blush CTE names. Comments are a neutral grey at APCA Lc 51. No purple keyword (the One Dark / Tokyo Night / Catppuccin signature) and no green-string + blue-function recipe.
themes.da1Notes: DA1: bg moved from h 311 / C 0.045 to h 317 / C 0.059 (ΔE 8.4 from Rosé Pine, 9.4 from Catppuccin Mocha, 11.5 from Damson). Lavender accent and orchid keyword dropped (orchid was ΔE 3.1 from One Dark Pro's keyword, lavender type 0.8 from Catppuccin lavender, peach constant 0.6 from Macchiato peach).
themes.statesNotes: Only ok (#73ce95 -> lighter #89d49a) and info (#72bdda -> #6abad9) move: success/error for deuteranopes 6.5 -> 8.4, info/success for tritanopes 5.2 -> 8.4; warn and err stay. Toast/banner 12 %, Run 8/11/14 %, Stop 6.5/11.5/16 %. TEST becomes orchid #dba9e6 because the shared violet sat 6 from the violet accent. Neutral steps lift inside the violet ink and keep its chroma (#3b2343 → #472f50). The primary is the one dark fill with a light label on a near-black surface: darkening would sink it into the ink, so it lifts to a brighter royal violet (#7751ca → #7c5ad8) and stops where the label still holds 4.66:1; danger deepens. Focus stays the lavender accent (ΔE 23 from the primary fill, ≥ 3.9:1 on every surface and selection fill); disabled opacity 0.42 because this highest-contrast theme lands at the same ~3.3:1 disabled label with less opacity. Critic: pressed stays at hover's lightness and turns a deeper ink violet (C .08) so text-err and the lavender text-accent keep >= 4.55 (were 4.09 / 4.12). Warning squiggle #cca700 so it is not the @parameter yellow (#e3ce77, dE 6.7 from warn).

themes.name: Damson
themes.identity: Damson-wine dusk (h 5, L 0.27, the lightest of the darks) with a pastel rose accent, rose keywords and honey strings: an orchard palette, not a candy one.
themes.eyeComfort: The lowest contrast of the darks (text at 11.9:1) and the lightest background, which suits a dim room. The accents are pastel (chroma 0.10 or less), not candy-bright.
themes.notes: err is pushed to vermilion (h 30) to stay ΔE 20 from the rose accent. The selection is violet (h 315), not raspberry: a raspberry selection read like a removed-line diff tint. The surface ladder is kept compact (hover at L 0.326) so the dark-family env tags stay at about 4.5:1 on hover.
themes.sqlNotes: Orchard palette on damson-wine: rose keywords (the accent family), honey strings, lilac functions, aqua numbers, greengage constants, peach-tan types and sky parameters; pale-ice CTE names and sage schema prefixes. Strings are not green and functions are not blue, so it no longer reads as Catppuccin on plum. The comment is a cool grey at APCA Lc 48.5, the most the rose keyword allows under deutan simulation.
themes.da1Notes: DA1: bg moved from plum h 347 to damson-wine h 5 (Inkwell now ΔE 11.5 / 48° away). SQL palette re-designed: mint strings and periwinkle functions were Catppuccin Mocha's green #a6e3a1 (ΔE 3.6) and blue #89b4fa (ΔE 1.8).
themes.statesNotes: Err warms to coral #ff8e7c (lighter, so it keeps 4.72:1 on its 12 % tint over the rose raised surface, was 4.19), warn brightens to #f9c764 and ok to #73dea4: warn/err deutan 8.5 -> 10.5, info/ok tritan 5.6 -> 8.5. Error rows 13 %, Run 8/11/14 %, Stop 4.5/9/13.5 % (coral has the least headroom on this red undertone); env words and the Production stripe, which failed on the rose selected row, now reach >= 4.63:1 there. A straight lightness step toward the greyer hairline turned the hover dusty grey, so the neutral hover rises to a richer wine instead (#562e35, C .059; pressed #633941; border #634a4f). The rose primary has a dark label: hover and pressed go lighter and paler (#f9b0d2 → #ffc4df), blush rather than candy; danger deepens. Focus is the accent lifted and cooled to orchid-rose #f2afdb: against the coral error the plain accent fell to tritan ΔE 8.8, this keeps ≥ 12.8 in every CVD simulation. Critic: button pressed deepens to a richer wine at hover's lightness (err 4.29 -> 4.56, muted 3.98 -> 4.56). Warning squiggle #e3cf55, a lemon-amber: warn #f9c764 sat dE 4.1 from the string token #e4bc64 (a warning under a string literal looked like part of the string); tritan separation from the error squiggle 13.9 -> 18.3.

themes.name: Juniper
themes.identity: Evergreen pine (h 151) with a sunlit-lime accent and parchment-tinted text: the one green dark, with a lively primary button that is still not neon.
themes.eyeComfort: Green-grey surfaces sit in the lowest-strain hue band, and text is at 12.0:1. The lime accent stays at chroma 0.13 and is used only for focus, the active tab and the primary button.
themes.notes: ok is jade (h 168), not lime, ΔE 19.5 from the accent, so 'success' never looks like 'focused'. The selection is slate-blue (h 255): a green selection read as a diff-insert tint. warn is orange (h 65), well away from the lime accent.
themes.sqlNotes: Lime keywords (h 124, the accent's family) with a tamed-Dracula spread on pine: pink functions, aqua strings, lilac numbers, peach constants, khaki types, periwinkle parameters and sage operators. Comments are a grey with a trace of green, at 6.7:1, and CTE names a pale sky.
themes.da1Notes: DA1: bg hue 165 -> 151 so it no longer shares the blue-green band with Fathom (ΔE 8.6 -> 11.4).
themes.statesNotes: Info lightens to #94c9e8 and warn yellows to #f8b05e: info vs the teal-green ok for tritanopes 5.6 -> 8.4, warn/err tritan 8.1 -> 10.4; ok and err keep their round-1 hexes. Toast/banner 12 %, Run 8/12.5/17 %, Stop 7.5/10.5/13 %; DEV is teal-green #50d2a7, 19 from the lime accent. Neutral steps lift within the pine green and keep its chroma (#273f2e → #324b38, border #425346). The lime primary has a dark label, so it brightens toward sunlit lime and pales slightly when pressed (#bfe180 → #d5f098) instead of sliding to olive; danger deepens. Focus stays the lime accent: ≥ 4.7:1 everywhere, deutan ΔE 10.8 from the error colour, ΔE 55 in normal vision. Critic: pressed keeps hover's lightness and deepens into pine (C .056) instead of lifting (err 3.88 -> 4.57). Warning squiggle #cca700: deutan dE from the error squiggle 12.2 -> 15.0, tritan 10.4 -> 12.5.

themes.name: Floe
themes.identity: Clear-morning sea-ice white: an off-white with a faint sea-glass tint (h 197), slate-ink text and a deep teal accent.
themes.eyeComfort: The background at OKLCH L 0.963 (about 90 % luminance, not 100 %) cuts glare. Text is 13.5:1 instead of 21:1, and the cool tint stays crisp without the hospital-white feel.
themes.notes: A plain cool white was not possible. Every neutral or blue off-white with OKLCH L between 0.93 and 0.985 sits within ΔE 5 of #ffffff, Ayu Light, Light Owl or Catppuccin Latte. A cyan-leaning tint clears all of them: ΔE 6.0 or more to every main inspiration background (6.1 to Latte, 6.5 to #ffffff) and 5.6 to GitHub's #f6f8fa panel. The current line is stepped just 2.2 ΔE below the background so the selection still has room inside the light syntax window (layer luminance ≥ 0.77). info is azure (h 255), separate from the teal accent.
themes.sqlNotes: Teal-petrol keywords (h 205, the accent's family; ΔE 27 from Querithm Light's indigo) with violet functions, raspberry numbers, green strings, olive types, deep indigo constants and rust parameters. CTE names are a harbor blue (ΔE 18 from the ink identifiers), operators a slate violet, comments a warm grey.
themes.da1Notes: DA1: renamed (Glacier is an existing Sublime Text scheme with VS Code/Vim ports and is bundled in iTerm2-Color-Schemes, so it shows in Ghostty/Windows Terminal theme lists). Keyword moved from harbor blue to teal-petrol so it no longer shares Querithm Light's blue-keyword look; CTE names take the blue. v2: id renamed glacier -> floe (nothing has shipped); no editor or terminal theme named Floe was found.
themes.statesNotes: On these light surfaces every status hue must sit at OKLCH L <= 0.48 to keep 4.5:1 on raised, so the colour-blind gaps can only come from lightness and blue content: err becomes a deep crimson #900d30 (L 0.42), warn an ochre #805000, ok a jade #006444, info #135aa7 (warn/err deutan 4.5 -> 10.4, ok/warn protan 6.5 -> 12.2). Toast/banner 10 % with a 60 % border (crimson at 10 % over the cyan raised turns grey-mauve, so the border carries the hue), error rows 18 % so they read rose instead of grey; Run 4.5/9.5/14 %, Stop 5/8.5/10.5 %; PROD word and stripe crimson #900d2e, STAGING #805500, LOCAL near-neutral slate. Light, so every step shades darker: the neutral hover settles to the hairline's lightness with a touch more sea-glass chroma (#bfd5d4 → #b0c5c5) and the border darkens to #a8b8bc. The deep-teal primary has a light label, so it deepens (#006071 → #005261, label 6.9–8.5:1), which also firms its edge on the pale surfaces; danger deepens. Focus stays the accent teal (≥ 3.56:1 on every surface and selection fill); disabled opacity 0.55, because 0.45 leaves a disabled label at 2.5:1 on this pale ice. Critic: the darker hover steps pushed text-accent (Connect..., Export chart) to 4.25 and the server name's text-muted to 4.43 while merely hovered; hover is now one step lighter and pressed keeps that lightness and turns clearer sea-glass (C .04) instead of darker, so every button label stays >= 4.55 in every state. Warning squiggle back to the round-1 light mark #a87000: it is lighter than the crimson error squiggle (luminance ratio 1.34 -> 2.18; deutan dE 10.4 -> 21.9).

themes.name: Vellum
themes.identity: Warm bisque paper (h 58, C 0.026) with sepia-brown ink and a mulberry accent: it reads like a book page, not a screen.
themes.eyeComfort: The bisque paper (L 0.957, about 87 % luminance) keeps the lowest blue-light share of the light themes (CIE Z 0.76× white). Sepia text is at 12.6:1, and the selection is a cool grey-blue wash that is clearly visible (ΔE 11.5) without a saturated highlighter.
themes.notes: The accent is mulberry (h 340) rather than orange, so it never collides with warn (ochre, h 70) or err (brick, h 28). The selection stays off the red and green axes so it can never be mistaken for a diff tint. ident (object names) is deep teal, for a second ink colour beside the sepia text.
themes.sqlNotes: Ink on vellum: mulberry keywords (the accent's family, darker), ink-blue functions, olive strings, rust numbers, teal types, violet-indigo constants (the grid's NULL) and ochre parameters, with sepia operators. CTE names are petrol blue and schema prefixes a cool slate against the warm sepia text.
themes.da1Notes: DA1: the v1 cream #f8f1df was ΔE 1.1 from Solarized Light's #fdf6e3 and moved to apricot #fdead8. v2: the apricot read peachy, so the paper is bisque #ffede0 (C 0.026; ΔE 6.8 from Solarized Light, 5.1 from Rosé Pine Dawn, 7.3 from Solarized base2). With C ≤ 0.03 every cream hue (h 70–100) sits within ΔE 5 of Solarized Light/base2, Gruvbox Light or Rosé Pine Dawn, so the paper leans to bisque, and the surfaces keep its chroma so the sidebar does not read peach.
themes.statesNotes: Same light-theme constraint as Floe: err #af2a24 -> deep crimson #8b162c (19.7 from the plum accent), warn #805000, ok jade #006444 (the olive #306922 merged with warn for protanopes at 3.9 -> now 12.2), info #1c5ba1. Toast/banner 10 % + 60 % border; error rows 18 % because at 10 % the error row matched the dusty-pink selected row (2.6 -> 4.2); Run 5/8.5/12 %, Stop 5/9/13 %; TEST is a bluer violet #5546af to stay 19 from the plum accent. Light paper: steps shade darker into warm taupe (#d7c8bb → #c9b9ad, border #c1ab9b), never grey. The mulberry primary has a light label, so it deepens like ink soaking in (#7a2b64 → #6b1e57, label 8.4–10.2:1); danger deepens. Focus is the accent turned 10° bluer (#884183) so a focused field stays clearly apart from a crimson error border (ΔE ≥ 22.7 normal, ≥ 16 in every CVD simulation); disabled opacity 0.55, since 0.45 gives only 2.5:1 on paper. Critic: as Floe; text-accent was 4.06 on the button hover and text-muted 4.40 on the toolbar hover. Hover is lighter warm taupe, pressed keeps its lightness and warms toward rosy paper (C .032-.036). Warning squiggle #a87000: luminance ratio to the error squiggle 1.36 -> 2.22, deutan dE 10.5 -> 22.3.

themes.name: Querithm Dark
themes.identity: Today's Dark, unchanged: blue-black with a sky-blue accent.
themes.sqlNotes: Standard's nine roles and brackets are kept hex for hex. New roles: constant is a pastel rose #f8acb5 (a pale lilac next to the periwinkle keyword could not reach ΔE 15 from keyword and 12 from variable), CTE names a sky blue #8fd5ff (DA2: ΔE 18.9 from identifiers), schema prefixes a dim warm taupe #c5ac98 so the table name after the dot leads, and parameter = variable #e6a6d6 on purpose. Word operators stay bold.

themes.name: Querithm Light
themes.identity: Today's Light, unchanged: white with a cobalt accent.
themes.sqlNotes: Standard's nine roles and brackets are kept hex for hex. New roles: constant raspberry #832543, CTE cobalt #155ed0 (DA2: ΔE 29 from identifiers), schema taupe #6c5644, parameter plum #543763 (not = variable, because #8a1f7c sits ΔE 4.2 from the indigo keyword under protan). Standard's own keyword/variable (protan ΔE 4.16) and type/comment (deutan ΔE 5.98) stay below the CVD anchor floor; the checker reports them as pre-existing Standard pairs. Word operators stay bold.
